title: Introduction to Halves Using Rectangular Cut-outs

studentJourneyDraft.title: Introduction to Halves Using Rectangular Cut-outs
studentJourneyDraft.subject: Mathematics

steps.title: Welcome!
steps.purpose: Greet the child and set emotional tone
steps.owlText: Hello friend! Today we are going to learn something exciting. We will learn about halves!
steps.studentText: Today we learn about halves. A half is one of two equal parts!

media.altText: Owl teacher waving hello with a rectangle shape beside it
media.fallbackText: Hello friend! Today we learn about halves.

steps.title: Our Mission
steps.purpose: Tell the child what they will learn in child-friendly language
steps.studentText: Today you will learn what a half is. A half means one of two equal parts of something whole.

steps.title: Think First!
steps.purpose: Activate prior knowledge about sharing and equal parts
steps.owlText: Before we start, think about this: If you have one chapati and you want to share it fairly with your friend, how would you cut it?
steps.studentText: How would you share one chapati fairly with a friend? Think about it!

media.altText: A whole chapati with a question mark above it
media.fallbackText: Think about sharing one chapati fairly with a friend.

steps.title: Learn It
steps.purpose: Teach the core concept: what is a half
steps.owlText: When we cut something into two equal parts, each part is called a half. Look at this rectangle. I will fold it into two equal parts. Each part is one half. We write it as 1/2.
steps.studentText: A half means one of two equal parts. When you fold a paper into two equal parts, each part is one half. We write: 1/2

media.altText: A rectangle being folded into 2 equal parts. One part is shaded. Shows 1/2.
media.caption: One half. We write it as 1/2.
media.fallbackText: A rectangle divided into 2 equal parts. One part is shaded. This is one half. We write it as 1/2.

steps.title: Real Life Connection
steps.purpose: Connect halves to real life — Kenyan context
steps.owlText: We see halves every day! When you cut a chapati into two equal pieces, each piece is one half. When you fold a paper into two equal parts, each part is one half. Halves are all around us!
steps.studentText: Happens every day! A chapati cut into 2 equal pieces. Each piece is one half. A paper folded into 2 equal parts. Each part is one half.

media.altText: A chapati cut into 2 equal halves. A paper folded into 2 equal parts.
media.caption: Halves in real life: chapati and paper folding.
media.fallbackText: A chapati cut into 2 equal pieces. Each piece is one half.

steps.title: Watch and Learn
steps.purpose: Show a worked example of identifying halves
steps.owlText: Let me show you. This rectangle is divided into 2 equal parts. One part is shaded. The shaded part is one half of the whole rectangle. We write it as 1/2. Both parts are the same size — that is what makes them equal.
steps.studentText: This rectangle has 2 equal parts. One part is shaded. The shaded part is 1/2. Both parts are the same size.

media.altText: A rectangle divided into 2 equal parts. Left part is shaded. Arrow points to shaded part labeled 1/2.
media.caption: The shaded part is one half. We write: 1/2
media.fallbackText: A rectangle divided into 2 equal parts. One part is shaded. This is one half. We write: 1/2.

steps.title: Your Turn!
steps.purpose: Child practices identifying which shape shows halves — different from QC
steps.owlText: Now it is your turn! Look at these two shapes. One shape is divided into two equal parts. The other is not. Which shape shows halves? Tap the correct one.
steps.studentText: Which shape is divided into 2 equal parts? Tap the shape that shows halves.

media.altText: Two shapes side by side. Shape A: rectangle divided into 2 equal parts. Shape B: rectangle divided into 2 unequal parts.
media.fallbackText: Two rectangles. One has 2 equal parts. One has 2 unequal parts. Which shows halves?

interaction.question: Which shape shows halves?
options: Shape A — the parts are equal
Shape B — the parts are not equal
interaction.correctAnswer: Shape A — the parts are equal
interaction.feedbackCorrect: Yes! Shape A has two equal parts. That is what makes it halves. The parts must be the same size!
interaction.feedbackIncorrect: Look carefully. Halves means the parts must be the same size. Which shape has two equal parts?

steps.title: Quick Check!
steps.purpose: Test understanding of halves — fraction identification
steps.owlText: Quick check! This circle is divided into 2 equal parts. One part is shaded. What fraction is shaded? Choose the correct answer.
steps.studentText: This circle is divided into 2 equal parts. One part is shaded. What fraction is shaded?

media.altText: A circle divided into 2 equal parts. One part is shaded.
media.fallbackText: A circle divided into 2 equal parts. One part is shaded.

interaction.question: What fraction is shaded?
interaction.feedbackCorrect: Correct! One out of two equal parts is one half. We write it as 1/2. Excellent work!
interaction.feedbackIncorrect: Not quite. Count the equal parts. There are 2. One part is shaded. That is one half. We write it as 1/2. Try again!

steps.title: Think About Your Learning
steps.purpose: Help the child reflect on what they learned
steps.owlText: You did great today! Think about what you learned. What is a half? When something is divided into two equal parts, each part is one half.
steps.studentText: What did you learn about halves today? A half means one of two equal parts.

interaction.question: How do you feel about halves today?

steps.title: You Did It!
steps.owlText: Wonderful! You learned about halves today. A half means one of two equal parts. You can find halves in chapati, paper, and many things around you. Keep practicing!
steps.studentText: You learned about halves! A half is one of two equal parts. Look for halves around you!

media.altText: Celebration with stars and a badge that says "I know halves!"
media.fallbackText: Wonderful! You learned about halves today!
